rules.justification: ADR 0001: the replay creates no command and no acknowledgement. The pending resolution continues, and PUBREC goes to the connection that is current when it completes.

ADR 0001: a client may not resend on a live connection (MQTT 5, section 4.4), and nothing it sends can restart a stalled admission. The packet is absorbed like a replay: the exchange already owns its admission, and the only answer owed is the PUBREC of its resolution.
ADR 0001: the deadline starts a resolution and arms the next deadline in the same transition, so that a resolution whose answer is held or lost is followed by another.
ADR 0001: each further deadline of an unresolved operation starts another resolution under a new EffectId and arms the next deadline.
ADR 0001: a deadline for an operation that became terminal is ignored as stale. Its token is never reused.

ARC-011: an unknown PUBREL follows an explicit protocol rule and makes no publication. MQTT 5 answers PUBCOMP with Packet Identifier not found.
ARC-011: a late return of an old operation does not end, start or acknowledge an exchange.
The slot holds no exchange, so no result can belong to it: a result is correlated to an effect the owner emitted for an exchange it holds (ADR 0003).

No PUBREC of this exchange was ever made eligible, so a conforming client cannot send its PUBREL. The connection is closed for the protocol error; the admission keeps its operation and its resolution continues. Answering PUBCOMP would end an exchange whose admission may yet commit.
ARC-011: a certain refusal ends the exchange without distribution and answers as the protocol says, with a PUBREC that carries a failure.
ARC-011: an unknown result keeps the operation and reconciles. The answer publishes nothing: the deadline armed with the resolution starts the next one (ADR 0001).

S0 retires no identity space: collection is outside the profile, and the closing of an epoch at restart answers RejectedCertain. RetiredOutcomeUnavailable cannot be reported for an operation the slot still waits for.
ARC-011: a late return of an old operation must not end the new exchange. The commit it reports is reconciled by the command machine.
ARC-011: the late result of the release of an earlier exchange does not touch the exchange that reuses its Packet Identifier.
A release is created only from AwaitPubrel, by the PUBREL of the exchange: before that no release of this exchange exists whose result could arrive.

DEM-010: knowledge is monotonic. The admission of the exchange is known committed; a repeated commit or an answer after collection changes nothing and acknowledges nothing again.
DEM-010: two contradictory terminal results for one recipe are an internal fault, with a stop and a diagnostic.
ADM-006: during the exchange a PUBLISH creates no second publication. After its PUBREL a client may only resend PUBREL, so the connection is closed for the protocol error and the release continues.
ADM-005 and ACK-001: a replayed PUBREL asks for no second release and gets no PUBCOMP before the release is known committed. PUBCOMP goes to the connection that is current when the release completes.
DEM-010: the admission of the exchange is known committed; no later answer about an admission changes the release in progress.

DEM-009: after a certain refusal a new preparation gets another OperationId and keeps the logical request. The exchange is still durably open, the client is owed a PUBCOMP only after a commit, and on a live connection it will not send PUBREL again.
An unknown result keeps the release and reconciles; nothing is published by the answer itself.
